title: Don't Overlook the Power of a Good Chap
author: Marriott, James
summary: James Marriott argues that the 21st century has catastrophically over-indexed on intellect while under-indexing temperament, character, and steadiness of spirit. The venture capital celebration of the 'unreasonable misfit' and Silicon Valley worship of socially broken genius amount to a culture dignifying its own dysregulation. Institutions actually run on boring virtues—reliability, honesty, good judgment, steadiness under pressure. As artificial intelligence makes raw cleverness cheap, what remains scarce is exactly what meritocratic culture stopped cultivating: trustworthy character formation.
points: The 21st century has grotesquely over-indexed on intellect while drastically under-indexing temperament, character, and steadiness of spirit.
Venture capital celebrates the unreasonable misfit; Silicon Valley worships the socially broken genius; both amount to dignifying dysregulation as talent.
Institutions run on boring virtues—reliability, honesty, good judgment, steadiness—virtues meritocratic culture now treats as quaint.
As AI makes raw cleverness cheap, what remains scarce is what stopped being cultivated: the formation of a person you can actually trust.
The most competent institutions are those that prioritize character formation and the cultivation of reliable human virtue over raw cognitive ability.
quotes: The twenty-first century has grossly over-indexed on intellect and grossly under-indexed on temperament, character, and steadiness of spirit.
Institutions actually run on the boring virtues of reliability, honesty, good judgment, and the capacity to keep an even keel under pressure.
Those virtues were once cultivated by the institutions that now treat them as quaint.

As artificial intelligence makes raw cleverness cheap, what will remain scarce is exactly what a meritocratic culture stopped teaching: the formation of a person you can actually trust.” Archived from The Times on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
